summary: Hourly-window smoothing patch deferred reserve-credit allocation and caused credits to be attributed to parent account instead of subaccount
description:
Issue summary:
Greenline noticed a lower-than-expected reserve-credit allocation for a set of subaccounts after our recent hourly-window smoothing algorithm patch. Credits were deferred and then applied to the parent org's invoice lines instead of the individual subaccount lines, causing one subaccount to receive an unexpectedly high finalized charge and the parent to show surplus provisional credits.

Impact:
- One subaccount billed ~USD 4,200 higher than expected on the finalized invoice for 2026-02-28 to 2026-03-01.
- Parent org shows a +USD 4,200 provisional credit that customer expects to be applied to the affected subaccount.
- Customer accounting delayed monthly close; finance cannot reconcile split invoices.

Environment:
- Dedicated account (Greenline Analytics) on prod us-east region.
- Reserve-credit smoothing feature rolled 2026-03-09 at 03:00 UTC via charging-service v1.12.

Steps to reproduce (customer reported):
1) Run multi-tenant batch embed job across two subaccounts at 02:47 UTC on 2026-03-09.
2) Observe postbacks delivered in-order to postback-reconciler, but hourly smoothing algorithm deferred reserve allocation into parent buffer.
3) Finalized invoices for period 2026-02-28 to 2026-03-01 show credits applied at parent level.

Logs / Observations:
- Postback-reconciler logs show "smoothing-window: apply-later" for hour window 02:00-03:00.
- Charging-service emitted reserve_credit_event with target_org_id set to parent_org_id for several postbacks that included subaccount tags.
- No evidence of duplicate postbacks or retry loops.

Initial hypothesis:
A change in hourly-window smoothing logic (PR #3421) introduced a race where multi-tenant postback aggregation ran a parent-level reduction pass before the subaccount attribution step, causing the reserve-credit allocator to mark credits as eligible for parent-level consolidation. Edge-case appears when subaccount postbacks arrive within the smoothing holding window and are processed after the parent reduction job.

Requested customer outcome:
- Clear explanation and timeline of credit allocation.
- Immediate provisional adjustment (credit reallocation) for the affected subaccount pending root-cause.
- Preventive action or rollback if this affects other accounts.

investigation_notes: Checked postback ordering: sequences for rq_9a8b7c/d show arrival timestamps within 12s of each other and within smoothing window holdback.
Charging-service change (PR #3421) introduced an optimization that short-circuits attribution map merge under high load; this optimization incorrectly uses parent org id as fallback key.
No evidence of customer-side mis-tagging; bank of examples include proper subaccount_id field in postbacks.
Runbook cross-check: existing reserve-reallocation playbook assumes postback-reconciler has atomic attribution step; that assumption broken by new optimization.
Simulated replay of postbacks with current patch reproduces misattribution in 42% of trials under timing variance similar to customer's traffic spike.
resolution_notes: Temporary workaround applied: manually created an invoice credit reallocation for subaccount-analytics-3 equal to USD 4,200 on 2026-03-12; customer notified and shown pending adjustment on console.
Engineering to land fix reverting short-circuit fallback and restoring attribution-first ordering (target deploy 2026-03-15, charging-service v1.12.1).
Add integration test to charging-service CI to cover subaccount vs parent consolidation ordering and smoothing holdback behavior.
Post-deploy action: run mapper across affected time range (2026-03-09 02:00 - 03:00 UTC) to re-evaluate credits for other customers and queue reallocation jobs where appropriate.
Follow-up: schedule a customer postmortem and provide formal remediation timeline and any billing waivers if additional affected invoices discovered.
